segments.name: QNX
segments.description: Supplies safety-certified operating systems, hypervisors, middleware and development tools, Radar telematics and Certicom cryptography to automakers and industrial customers.
segments.evidence: QNX consists of BlackBerry® QNX®, BlackBerry Radar®, BlackBerry® Certicom®, and other QNX applications.

segments.name: Secure Communications
segments.description: Sells certified encrypted voice, messaging and file-sharing, critical event management and endpoint management software to governments, militaries and enterprises.
segments.evidence: Secure Communications consists of BlackBerry® UEM, BlackBerry® AtHoc® and BlackBerry® SecuSUITE®.

segments.name: Licensing
segments.description: Monetizes the company's patent portfolio through intellectual property arrangements and settlement awards.
segments.evidence: Licensing consists of the Company's intellectual property arrangements and settlement awards.

revenueModel.text: Customers pay software licence, royalty, support and maintenance fees for QNX and secure communications software, and pay for intellectual property licensing.
revenueModel.evidence: QNX revenue is generated predominantly through volume-based royalties and through software licenses, commonly bundled with support, maintenance and professional services.

changes.text: The Cylance business was sold and its results are reported as discontinued operations, so it is no longer part of a reportable segment.
changes.evidence: As a result of the Cylance sale, it is no longer reported alongside UEM, SecuSUITE and AtHoc as the Cybersecurity segment.

changes.text: From fiscal 2025, UEM, SecuSUITE and AtHoc are reported as the Secure Communications segment.
changes.evidence: Effective from the fiscal year ended February 28, 2025, those three businesses are reported separately from Cylance as the Secure Communications segment.
